title: A Story from My Past
writingModel: A Night I Will Never Forget — by Amir Bekzhanov

It was a cold November evening. The temperature was dropping and the wind was blowing hard outside my dormitory window. I was sitting at my desk, working on a programming essay. The deadline was in three hours and I was feeling increasingly stressed. Everything was quiet — I was the only one awake on my floor, or so I thought.

At exactly 11:47 p.m., the power went out. One second I was typing the conclusion of my essay, and the next second my screen went completely black. I sat in the dark for a moment, not understanding what had happened. Then I grabbed my phone. The group chat was already exploding with messages.

While I was reading the messages, I heard voices in the corridor. Students were coming out of their rooms — some were laughing, some were complaining, and some were carrying blankets. I put on my jacket and went out. In the hallway, Kamila was telling everyone to stay calm. Zhibek had arrived with a thermos of tea. Rustam was already telling his first ghost story.

We sat on the floor for nearly two hours. The emergency lights gave everything an orange glow. Someone found candles. We talked, ate biscuits, and forgot completely about essays and deadlines. At one point, Kamila was describing blackouts in her village, and I realised I had never thought about how different our experiences were — her talking about candles as a normal part of winter, me never having lived without electricity for more than a few minutes.

When the power came back at 1:58 a.m., there was a cheer. I went back to my room and looked at my essay. I still needed to write the conclusion. But something had shifted. I sat down, wrote it in twenty-five minutes — probably the best twenty-five minutes of writing I had ever done — and went to sleep.

I will never forget that night. Not because of the blackout, but because of what happened in that hallway. We were all stressed, all behind on our work, all worried. But for two hours we were just people sitting together in the dark, and that turned out to be exactly what we all needed.
